hero.heading: Connecting experienced
hero.description: Together we build a successful study path. The Mentor Programme is a place where experienced students share knowledge and experience with first-year students.

information.title: Learn more
information.programContent: The Mentor Programme is a place where experienced students pass on their knowledge and experience to first-year students. The RSU Mentor Programme for Latvian students is implemented every year from September to February and is based on the principle of volunteering. Its aim is to promote the integration of new students into the academic and social life.
information.mentorContent: A Mentor is an adviser and helper for first-year students. It is a student who has started studies at least in the second year and is ready to share their knowledge and practical experience with new students. A Mentor can give advice and answer questions. One mentor can have up to 5 mentees.
information.menteeContent: Any first-year student can become a mentee. A Mentee is a student who wants to learn about the study process, opportunities for social life at the university, and wants to gain new contacts and experience.

testimonial.title: What participants say
testimonial.quote1: The first days at university can be described like this: 'Limitless opportunities, yet zero understanding of what to do with those opportunities and how to apply them in everyday life.' In this very context, the true key to success for the first steps of academic life is the Mentor Programme. A Mentor is that person you can always call or at least send a message to during intense classes and complicated assignments—not just as a colleague, but as a close friend.
testimonial.attribution1: — Georgs Pimanovs, Faculty of Medicine and Dentistry
testimonial.quote2: A year and a half ago, when I started my studies at Rīga Stradiņš University, my life seemed to turn 180 degrees. I found myself a mentor—a person who explains the organisation of any study course and various events. Thanks to this positive experience, I felt more confident in my studies. I am currently a mentor to three international students and two Latvian students, and I feel proud every time I can help them.
